ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a shaded triangle, with a right-angle mark at the lower left corner; the right-side vertex is labeled 18°; the side from the lower-left right-angle vertex to the right-side vertex is labeled 12 cm. Reasoning: Treat it as a right triangle. The 12 cm side is adjacent to the 18° angle, so the other leg is 12·tan(18°), and the hypotenuse is 12/cos(18°). The perimeter P = 12 + 12·tan(18°) + 12/cos(18°) ≈ 12 + 3.8990 + 12.6173 = 28.5163. Rounded to the hundredths place, it is 28.52.

raw_record.question_text: Find the perimeter of the triangle. Round to the nearest hundredth.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a right triangle: the lower-left angle has a right-angle marker, the angle at the right vertex is 18°, and the side between those two vertices is labeled 12 cm. Since the 12 cm side is adjacent to the 18° angle, use right-triangle trigonometry to find the other two sides: opposite leg = 12·tan(18°), hypotenuse = 12/cos(18°). Add all three side lengths to get the perimeter: P = 12 + 12·tan(18°) + 12/cos(18°), then round to the nearest hundredth.
